title: Prawn Laksa
subtitle: Malaysian coconut curry noodle soup with prawns
excerpt: A rich, fragrant coconut curry broth poured over rice noodles and topped with prawns, bean sprouts, and fresh herbs. One of the great dishes of Malaysian and Singaporean cooking.

recipe.sourceNotes: Laksa is a spicy noodle soup found across Malaysia, Singapore, and Indonesia, with many regional variants. The two main styles are curry laksa (coconut curry-based) and asam laksa (tamarind and fish-based, with no coconut). This recipe is curry laksa, the form most widely encountered outside Southeast Asia. Nyonya laksa from Malacca is one of the most celebrated variants: a rich coconut broth flavoured with a rempah (ground spice paste) containing lemongrass, galangal, and dried shrimp. The dish reflects the fusion of Chinese and Malay culinary traditions that defines Peranakan (Straits Chinese) cooking.

content.text: The laksa paste is the flavour core of the dish. If you are in a hurry, a good quality shop-bought laksa paste (available in Asian supermarkets) can be substituted for the home-made version, which reduces the prep to assembling the broth. Blending the paste to a smooth, fine consistency is important: large chunks of lemongrass or chilli in the finished broth are unpleasant. Do not boil the broth once the coconut milk is added: a simmer is enough, and boiling can cause the coconut milk to split.

items.preparation: dried, soaked in boiling water for 5 minutes, drained

content.text: Make the paste: put the lemongrass, galangal, shallots, garlic, chilli flakes, turmeric, and coriander in a blender. Add 3 tablespoons of water. Blend until smooth.

Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the paste and fry for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant and the oil separates. Add the stock and bring to a simmer. Cook for 10 minutes.
Add the coconut milk. Stir and heat gently without boiling. Add the prawns and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes until pink and cooked through. Season with fish sauce and lime juice. Taste and adjust.
Divide the soaked noodles between deep bowls. Ladle the broth and prawns over the top. Top with bean sprouts, sliced spring onion, and fresh coriander. Serve immediately with extra lime wedges.
